I'm an advanced seamstress. I made view C in size 8 (ease was 5" over body measurements): to fit 36" bust, 28" waist, 36" hips. I am 5'9" tall and didn't lengthen or shorten any pieces.

The pattern was well-written and designed to have a fully-lined bodice. The pattern also included instructions for installing an invisible zipper, which (while obvious and unnecessary to the more advanced seamstress) would be helpful to someone relatively new to sewing. This pattern would probably suit an intermediate level of sewing skill; the waistband and skirt may be a little tricky for a beginner to sew along the curves nicely.

Changes:

  • I used a color block fabric scheme, instead of the pattern recommendation.

  • I didn't cut out or use the neck edge facing/interfacing pieces. The dress holds up just fine without it.

  • I serged the skirt together, and I also serged the skirt onto the bodice/waistband portion.

  • I fully lined the skirt as well.

  • I hemmed the skirt and skirt lining using a blind-hem stitch instead of narrow-hem.

Highly recommend this pattern! I'm actually using the skirt pieces on a different bodice for my current project, simply because the skirt hangs nicely and doesn't take up a lot of fabric yardage.
